title: v0 by Vercel — UI Prototyping at the Speed of Thought

sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

By the end of this lesson you'll be able to generate production-quality UI components and full page layouts from text descriptions using v0.dev, and integrate them into a project.

## What is v0.dev?

v0.dev is Vercel's AI UI generator. You describe a component or page in plain English, and it generates clean React code using **shadcn/ui** and **Tailwind CSS** — the same components used by modern production apps.

**v0 vs Bolt:**
- **Bolt** builds full applications — backend, routing, data, all in one
- **v0** specialises in UI — it generates beautiful components and layouts, ready to drop into any React project

Use v0 when:
- You need a specific UI component fast (a pricing table, a nav bar, a data table)
- You're building a React app and want production-quality components without writing CSS
- You want to prototype a page layout before writing the real code
- You're exploring design options and want to see 3 variations quickly

## How to Use v0.dev

**Access:** Go to **v0.dev** — sign in with your Vercel or GitHub account. Free tier gives you a generous number of generations per month.

**Basic workflow:**
1. Describe the component or page you want
2. v0 generates 3 variations
3. Select the one closest to what you want
4. Chat to refine: "make the button red", "add a dark mode toggle", "replace the chart with a table"
5. Copy the code — it's clean, importable React

**What v0 generates:**
- React components with TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS classes for styling
- shadcn/ui components (pre-built accessible components)
- Responsive layouts that work on mobile and desktop
- The code is production-quality — not demo code

## Prompting v0 Effectively

v0 responds best to prompts that describe the visual outcome, the data it shows, and the user interaction.

**Weak prompt:**
> A dashboard

**Strong prompt:**
> A SaaS analytics dashboard. Left sidebar with navigation (Overview, Users, Revenue, Settings). Main content area shows: a top stat row with 4 KPI cards (total revenue, active users, conversion rate, churn). Below that, a line chart (revenue over 30 days) and a data table (recent signups: name, email, plan, date, status). Dark theme.

**Elements of a strong v0 prompt:**
- Layout structure (sidebar, tabs, grid, sections)
- What data is displayed and where
- Interaction states (hover, selected, empty state)
- Visual style (dark/light, minimal/detailed)
- The specific component type (card, table, chart, form, modal)

sections.title: Build a Landing Page with v0
sections.content:
Use v0 to generate a complete landing page for a real product or project.

**Step 1 — Define what you're building a landing page for:**
- Your portfolio site
- A side project or tool you've built
- A hypothetical product (practice counts)
- Your freelance services

**Step 2 — Write your v0 prompt:**
```
A landing page for [product name]. 

Hero section: headline "[your main value proposition]", subheadline, 
primary CTA button "[action]" and secondary "[action]". 

Features section: 3 features with icons, title, description.
Pricing section: 3 tiers (Free, Pro $29/mo, Team $99/mo) with feature lists.
Footer: links to Features, Pricing, Blog, Contact.

[Light/dark] theme. Clean, modern, professional.
```

**Step 3 — Generate and pick the best variation.**

**Step 4 — Iterate on specifics:**
- "Change the primary color from blue to indigo"
- "The hero image placeholder should be replaced with a code editor screenshot mockup"
- "Make the pricing cards highlight the Pro tier as recommended"

**Step 5 — Copy the code.** Click the code tab, copy all.

**Step 6 — Drop it into Bolt:** Paste the component into a new Bolt project as the starting point for a full working site. Ask Bolt to add a working contact form and deploy it.

**End result:** A professional landing page, generated in under 30 minutes.

sections.title: Workshop A — Component Sprint: 5 Components in 25 Minutes
sections.content:
Build intuition for v0 by generating 5 different component types quickly.

For each, write a specific prompt and generate the component. Note what works and what needs refinement.

**Component 1 (5 min): Data table**
Prompt: "A data table showing employees: name, department, role, start date, status (active/inactive). Sortable columns, search input, pagination, row actions (edit, delete). Clean, minimal."

**Component 2 (5 min): Navigation bar**
Prompt: "A top navigation bar for a SaaS app. Left: logo + product name. Centre: nav links (Dashboard, Projects, Team, Reports). Right: notifications bell, avatar with dropdown (Profile, Settings, Log out). Sticky on scroll. Light theme."

**Component 3 (5 min): Settings page**
Prompt: "An account settings page. Left sidebar nav (Profile, Security, Notifications, Billing, Team). Main content shows Profile section: avatar upload, name, email, bio fields, save button. Clean form layout."

**Component 4 (5 min): Stats cards**
Prompt: "4 KPI stat cards in a row. Each has: icon (top left), metric name, large number, trend (% up/down with arrow), sparkline chart. Cards for: Revenue, New Users, Conversion Rate, Churn. Dark background cards."

**Component 5 (5 min): Empty state**
Prompt: "An empty state for a projects list. Illustration area (abstract shapes), heading 'No projects yet', subtext 'Create your first project to get started', primary button 'New Project'. Centered, friendly."

**Debrief:** Which component type did v0 handle best? Which needed the most iteration?

sections.title: Workshop B — v0 + Bolt: Full-Stack from UI First
sections.content:
Use v0 for the UI and Bolt to add functionality — the UI-first development workflow.

**Step 1 — Design in v0:** Build the UI for your app idea from Lesson 9-5 (or pick a new one). Focus on getting the layout and components right. Generate: the main screen, an empty state, and a modal or form.

**Step 2 — Export to Bolt:** Copy the v0 code. Open bolt.new, paste your v0 code as the starting point, and tell Bolt: "This is the UI for my app. Now add: [the data and logic the app needs]."

**Step 3 — Connect data:** Ask Bolt to wire up the UI to real data — local storage first, then a database if needed.

**Step 4 — Test the full flow:** Does data appear in the UI? Do the buttons do something? Can you complete the core user journey end to end?

**Step 5 — Deploy and share.** Get a live URL.

**Reflect:** How does this compare to starting in Bolt directly? Which approach felt more controlled?

sections.question: v0 generates a component using shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS. You want to use it in a plain HTML project (no React, no build step). What is the issue?
options: There is no issue — React code runs in any browser

v0's output requires a React environment and a build step (like Vite or Next.js) — it won't work pasted into a plain HTML file. You'd need to either set up a React project, use Bolt to run it, or ask v0 for a plain HTML/CSS version
You need to pay for v0 to get plain HTML
shadcn/ui components auto-convert to plain HTML
sections.explanation: v0 generates React components — JSX syntax and Tailwind utility classes. These can't be pasted into a plain HTML file and opened in a browser. To use v0 output you need a React project (Next.js, Vite + React, Create React App) with Tailwind configured. The workaround for plain HTML projects: ask v0 to 'Generate this as plain HTML and CSS with no framework dependencies', or use Bolt which handles the environment setup for you.

sections.content: **Lesson 9-6 complete.** v0.dev is now in your toolkit — describe a UI, get production-quality React code, iterate in chat. Combined with Bolt for functionality and Claude Code for depth, you have a complete rapid development stack. Next: Lovable for full product development from a single idea.
